P1.evidence: No setter notes, application or prior context referenced anywhere. The frame ran one of the four parts plus the disqualification promise: 'go into what you're actually trying to achieve with working on your fitness and mobility. See if we can help you out with actually getting to that goal. If we can, I'll take you through how. If not, that's really fine.' Nothing about where he is now, what is in the way, or what he needs. Agreement taken ('okay?' — 'Okay, cool') and the open question asked.

P2.evidence: Height and age asked directly; weight was volunteered in the opening sentence and never asked. Injuries were handled well and pursued — 'do you have any, like any pains, aches, mobility issues at the moment?', then 'Anything else?', then 'Any? Like stiffnesses or something?', and later 'What sort of bones have you broken? I do need to know that', which produced a substantial fracture history. Training week and results were both properly established, including how long the plateau had lasted and what he had tried since. Diet asked and mapped in detail. Work never asked — that he runs a company came out only as an aside about time. Health conditions, sleep and energy never touched at all.

P3.evidence: The surface goal was well established — Fight Club physique, abs, 10-12% body fat, not bulky. The bridge question was asked once, well: 'what's like the why for you behind that? I'm just curious, so many people are just okay with it.' The answer was 'just personal pride' and that is where it stopped. He was never asked what moving better would do for him, who else it impacts, or anything reaching kids, identity or legacy — and the man is 56, divorced, with grown children and 22 years of military service behind him. The rep then closed the loop against himself in his own summary: 'mainly just for personal pride, there's no big why for you behind it.' Naming the absence of a why and moving on is the decision that cost this call.

P4.evidence: 'Have you ever been like coached by someone to get to a specific goal?' produced the military history and the eight years since; 'what do you mean with just life?' pushed on the drift; 'Have you tried anything after that sort of happening to still continue going down?' worked the plateau properly; and 'what do you think is like the biggest roadblock that you have that we need to cross together?' let him name form and technique himself. The one miss is the one that mattered most: the scripted 'The information isn't the problem. Why can't you stick to it on your own?' was never used, against a prospect whose entire position was 'the information's out there, you know' — and whose honest answer would have been that he can stick to it on his own, which is exactly the disqualification the phase is designed to surface.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame does not appear anywhere in this transcript. He was never asked what the next two years look like if nothing changes, whether he is willing to settle for it, why not, or whether he is ready to draw a line. The phase carries 20 points of weight and was skipped entirely, which is why there was no accumulated cost of inaction to set against $6,000 when the price landed.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran twice before price — 'do you feel like if we double down on those things that you're actually going to be able to see some progression with us as well?' answered 'Absolutely. I think so. That's why I'm here', and then a 1-10 scale on whether the programme itself worked for him. But the scale question returned a conditional, not a yes: 'I think the program sounds fantastic. It always just comes down to what is the cost, right?' He ran a good Ferrari analogy to separate want from afford, got 'outside of the price, yeah', and went to the number — without ever asking the all-in question and without returning to a Phase 5 that had never been run.

P11.evidence: No agreement was reached on any tier, so none of the payment or onboarding steps became reachable. The rep did walk through what onboarding would look like at 00:39:18, and did state the sequencing correctly — 'I can just only book it in when we have done the payments' — but nothing was executed.

objection_plays.detail: The opening moves ran and ran well. Isolate: 'outside of the investments, would you be like, yeah, Richard, I just want to get this started?' Open conversation, close to verbatim: 'it's not something that's locked in on six grand instantly or whatever... if you want, we can have a conversation about it, see if we can make something work.' The worth question was asked repeatedly and correctly separated worth from possibility: 'if it's worth that for you, it's just not possible at the moment, then we're here to figure it out together.' What did not run: the SHOULD-I versus HOW reframe, the 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up' line, and five of the six financial-picture questions — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. 'What would be possible for you right now?' is the only one asked, and it produced a number the rep then simply discounted to twice.

'I always give myself 24 hours to think about stuff' triggered it at 00:54:20. The probing moves ran — what specifically he would think about, whether he would research or sleep, and whether anything more was needed from the rep — but the play's substance did not. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', and no identity move. Each probe was immediately followed by granting the delay: 'you're free to do that. You're free to do that.'

A cheaper alternative that genuinely worked, in its strongest possible form. He lost 68 lb in 18 months on free internet information with no coach and said so as the closing argument: 'I've lost 68 pounds purely on my own... I'm sitting here as a product of that. I just want to take it to the next level.' The named substitutes were YouTube, ChatGPT form review, three or four other kettlebell coaches on social media, and a personal friend who is a kettlebell personal trainer he estimates at $200/month. This is the exact gap already logged from the Badrane Hriouch call and there is still no play for it. The rep improvised two reasonable counters — 'Who's going to check your form?' and 'How much money do you think it's gonna cost if you injure yourself again?' — and the prospect had a credible answer to both.

Debt refusal. The rep offered third-party financing and the prospect refused it as a matter of principle rather than capacity: 'I just don't do stuff. If I can't afford it, don't pay for it. All my cars are paid for. They're paid for in cash.' Objection C's whole financial-picture sequence is built to find money that exists somewhere — credit, cards, investments — and has nothing to say to someone who will not use credit at all. The rep dropped it immediately and went to discounting instead.

notes: Baseline and Past Attempts were solid, and the money conversation opened correctly. Two things sank it. Phase 5 was skipped in its entirety, so no cost of inaction existed to weigh against the number. And in Phase 3 the rep asked the why question once, accepted 'personal pride', and then said in his own summary that there was no big why — at which point the sale had nothing underneath it. The coachable instruction is narrow: when a 56-year-old who has already lost 68 pounds alone says his motivation is pride, that is the beginning of the phase, not the end of it.
